summary: Produced the invoicing-domain ownership decision as ADR 0010 (docs/adr/0010-invoicing-plugin-ownership.md) after inspecting the delivered contract surface and the current plugin runtime: the invoice entities/commands/events are already frozen and ownership-independent; the runtime manifest is exactly 8 fields, plugins are fixed in settings.PMO_PLUGIN_MODULES, migrations run with the Django app and there is no URL/page registration point, so existing plugin pages are bound in pmo_plugins/delivery/urls.py. The ADR compares option A (new pmo_plugins.invoicing plugin app), B1/B2/B3 (fold into management_revenue / settlement / contracts or delivery) and C (defer), with criteria covering domain ownership and owner-read-model boundary, migration isolation/rollback, manifest/requires fit, route and command exposure, SDK/plugin-evolution compatibility, test/deploy/rollback cost and core growth. It decides option A: a new pmo_plugins.invoicing app as the invoice write owner, contract schema unchanged, contracts/settlement consumed only through named read-only interfaces; implementation constraints freeze the 8-field manifest (requires contracts/settlement, capabilities empty), an app-owned migration chain starting at 0001, delivery/urls root single-write binding, canonical invoicing.* commands staying browser/private-service-only in the first slice, and PH-252 remaining proposed until PH-150/PH-155 are done. PH-252's decision point now points at ADR 0010 and its exact per-file whitelist is unchanged. No scaffold, product code, migration or contract-schema change was made. The spec asked for a docs/v1.0-development record, but PH-259's BASE allowed_paths do not include that directory, so the decision is recorded in the ADR plus this report/handoff and the whitelist was not expanded.
